status_detail: DigiPowerX lists Hildebran, NC as a mega-site pipeline in its official footprint; local reporting says DigiPower X owns about 40 acres in Hildebran, including 199 Cline Park Court near a Duke Energy substation, and has signaled a 200 MW AI/data-center facility. Hildebran updated zoning in March 2026, but the town manager said no active zoning permit applications had been received and any future proposal would require conditional zoning.
notes: Kept as planned/early-stage, not approved, because accessible local reporting says no permit applications had been filed. Capacity from local reporting/company-linked materials; official company page confirms NC pipeline but not full local entitlement status.

status_detail: Segra lists Kannapolis among its owned/operated data center facilities; third-party and trade sources identify the facility at 465 Charles Babbage Lane in Kannapolis, formerly DataChambers/NorthState, with about 45,000-50,000 square feet and 2.4 MW fully built-out power. DCD reported the Segra-occupied Kannapolis data center was sold to a Landmark Dividend affiliate in 2021.
notes: Official Segra sources confirm the Kannapolis data center/address; MW from DataCenterMap specs. Separately, Google leased a large facility near the Rowan-Cabarrus line in 2026, but Kannapolis officials said it is warehousing/logistics and not a data center.

status_detail: Google's official data-center location page says it has been building in the Lenoir data center community since 2007 and has invested more than $4 billion in the region and state. notes: Official sources confirm operating campus and 2026 expansion investment, but accessible official pages did not provide a project MW number.

status_detail: Caldwell County EDC says the county is home to Google and CentriLogic data centers. CentriLogic's official Lenoir page describes an operating managed-services and colocation data center in Lenoir, and Dacentec facility pages list the secure data center at 801 Main Street NW with 23,500 square feet, diverse utility feeds, UPS protection, and a 1 MW backup generator.
notes: Dacentec opened in 2010 and was later acquired by CentriLogic; using capacity_mw null because the official source gives backup generator size, not facility IT load.
